note: Which of Board A's copper structures a Board B candidate inherits, decided explicitly so no routing decision is copied while calling the candidate independently generated. The SHA-256 of this file is bound into every candidate's derivation.

rules.rationale: Continuous internal ground planes on both inner layers are shared product architecture: the acoustic array's return-path and reference strategy, not a routing choice. Metrics that depend on plane presence are therefore NOT evidence of independent optimization, and no candidate claims them as such.

rules.application: These keepouts implement the via-mask ink-dam guardrail around solder-mask openings, so they are functions of PLACEMENT, not architecture. A candidate keeps only those whose extent intersects a requirement-fixed footprint (still anchored to true geometry) and deletes the rest as stale the moment parts move. The via-mask gate measuring the candidate's actual geometry remains the authority either way; the keepouts only steer the router.
rules.rationale: Inheriting a keepout anchored to a component position Board B no longer uses would both block usable area and fail to protect the component's new location.

unmatched_zone_policy: refuse: a zone this policy does not classify blocks candidate generation until the policy says what it is
